clue.text: Revolutionary post boxes are beginning to catch on at home

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the post word goes round what follows
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a post is a job or position
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A
the opening letter of catch
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A radical's post-boxes are starting to catch on in his own home.
explanation.walkthrough: A metric are is 100 square metres, hence A. The post word wraps A and C, and IN is added on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jacobins were the radical club of the French Revolution, so a Jacobin is a revolutionary.

clue.text: Quite special circles love sporting contests

indicators.note: to circle something is to surround it, so the first pair of words goes around the love letter

blocks.note: quite, as in 'just so'
S is the abbreviation for special
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Very special rings make a lovely sight at sporting events.
explanation.walkthrough: JUST plus S makes JUSTS; the O goes in after the J.
explanation.definitionFit: Jousts were mounted tilting matches between knights, a medieval form of sporting contest.

clue.text: Affected toff with cape mounted open carriage

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounted means going upwards, so the letters are read from the bottom up

blocks.note: a yah is an affected upper-class person, from their drawled 'yes'
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A posh twit with a cloak rides about in an open carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: A yah is British slang for a loud upper-class person, named for their way of saying 'yes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chay is a dialect form of chaise, a light open carriage for one or two people.

clue.text: Spoken about role of path in space

indicators.note: about means around, so the spoken word goes round the role word

blocks.note: spoken rather than written
a small role is a bit part

explanation.surface: Talking about one's part in a space mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoken about' tempts a sound-alike reading, but spoken is just the word ORAL wrapped round the role.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is the path of a body travelling around a planet or star, and orbital is its adjective.

clue.text: Old schoolma'am is hopeless, giving up Latin

indicators.note: giving something up means letting it go, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: a hopeless outlook is bleak
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: An elderly teacher despairs and abandons Latin lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: Beak is old British school slang for a teacher, and also for a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated slang uses beak for a schoolmaster or schoolmistress, so an old schoolma'am fits.

clue.text: Found one part of MIT

blocks.note: first meaning: to set up or establish
second meaning: one word of the name the initials stand for

explanation.surface: Someone has located a single component at a famous university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as the past tense of find; here it is the present-tense verb to establish. MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
explanation.definitionFit: To institute is to establish or set up; the I in MIT stands for this very word.

clue.text: Old-fashioned motto's repellent for IT person

indicators.note: something repellent drives things back, so the letters are sent backwards

blocks.note: a posy is an archaic word for a short motto inscribed in a ring, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: A quaint saying puts off someone working in computing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sysop is a system operator, the person who runs a computer system or bulletin board.

clue.text: Scottish bluffer even turned up in serial

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means flipped to read from the bottom upwards
in means placed inside, so the flipped word sits within the serial abbreviation

blocks.note: SER is the dictionary abbreviation for serial, split around the inserted word
even, as in 'even more', can mean yet
the rest of the abbreviation SER

explanation.surface: A Scots con artist shows up again in a long-running story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluffer' looks like a cheat, but it is the comparative of bluff, meaning steep. Stey is Scots for steep, so steyer is steeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep cliff, so bluffer means steeper, which in Scots is steyer.

clue.text: Christian Union on the radio so long

indicators.note: words heard over the radio are judged by their sound, not their spelling

blocks.note: CU is the usual abbreviation for Christian Union, and its two letters said aloud

explanation.surface: A student Christian group says farewell over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christian Union is the evangelical society found at most British universities, abbreviated CU.
explanation.definitionFit: 'See you' and 'so long' are both casual ways of saying goodbye.

clue.text: They establish ministries first of all in order to change society

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, taken here from the word all
to change words is to rearrange them, so the letters of the phrase are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of all
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Reformers set up government departments as their first priority to transform society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of all' reads as 'before anything else'; it really means the opening letter of all. 'Ministries' is the clergy sense, not government.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordainers confer holy orders, so they install people in the ministry of the church.

clue.text: Still following page in mag

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the still word is placed second, behind the page letter

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for page
still, as in 'not still done', means yet

explanation.surface: A still photo comes after the first page in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the still word after the page letter. 'Mag' is not a magazine but short for magpie.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyet is a Scots and northern dialect word for the magpie, also called a mag.

clue.text: Gold chain seen in stock exchange regularly

indicators.note: something seen in a place sits inside it, so the chain letters go inside
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for chain, the surveyor's unit of length
a stock exchange is a bourse, and its 2nd, 4th and 6th letters are kept

explanation.surface: A gold chain is spotted on the trading floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The stock exchange must first become bourse, the Continental word for it, before its alternate letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth pigment, and its colour is a dull golden yellow.

clue.text: Hazel's region say, is in US city

indicators.note: something that is in another thing is placed inside it

blocks.note: NY is New York, opened here around the inserted word
to say is to utter
the rest of NY

explanation.surface: A woman called Hazel's home area is, so to speak, in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazel' looks like a woman's name, but it is the nut tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuttery is a plantation of nut trees, so it is where hazels grow.

clue.text: Girl hit not embarrassed

blocks.note: Una is a girl's name
hit, past tense, means bashed

explanation.surface: A girl got hit but showed no shame about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unabashed is not ashamed or disconcerted, so not embarrassed.

clue.text: Newspaper perhaps inspires French group musician

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the newspaper takes the group inside

blocks.note: a Post is a newspaper, such as the Washington Post; 'perhaps' marks it as one example
parti is French for a political party
the rest of POST

explanation.surface: A newspaper motivates a French band's performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop artist' calls Warhol to mind, but here it means a pop music performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop artist is a performer of popular music, which makes them a kind of musician.

clue.text: Composer who's an angelic figure in Italy

blocks.note: a cherub is a winged child-angel
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A composer who is something of a cherub in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Luigi Cherubini was an Italian composer working in Paris, best known for the opera Médée.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubini (1760–1842) was an Italian-born composer of operas and church music.

clue.text: Brought back tea with last of black bread from the east

indicators.note: something brought back returns the way it came, so the letters run right to left
the last of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: tay is a dialect word for tea
the final letter of black

explanation.surface: Someone fetched tea plus the dark crust of an Eastern loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money here, not a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The kyat is the currency of Myanmar, and bread is slang for money, so it is eastern money.

clue.text: Grass in Canterbury? Double work repeatedly left for cutting

indicators.note: a letter marked for cutting is to be removed from the word
repeatedly says the removal happens more than once, to each copy of the doubled word

blocks.note: work is toil, written twice because it is doubled
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Is grass in a cathedral city's close twice the labour, again and again left for mowing?
explanation.walkthrough: Canterbury is not the English cathedral city but the region of New Zealand's South Island, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Toitoi is a tall native New Zealand grass, so it grows in the Canterbury region.

clue.text: Smack fished inshore, pole cast

indicators.note: fished suggests something hauled about and rummaged, so the letters are churned up
to cast off something is to throw it away, so the pole letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
S is south, one of the poles

explanation.surface: A small fishing boat worked close to shore, its pole cast out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like a fishing boat, fitting the surface, but it is slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Smack is a street slang name for heroin, the opioid drug.

clue.text: Spirited person holds record for violent fiction

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it within, so the spirited word goes round the record

blocks.note: a spunk is a plucky spirited person; split open after its first letter
platter is old slang for a gramophone record
the rest of SPUNK

explanation.surface: A lively person keeps a dossier on violent novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like a file or entry, but it is a vinyl disc, or platter.
explanation.definitionFit: Splatterpunk is a genre of horror fiction marked by explicit, graphic gore and violence.

clue.text: ID includes first of many babies

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so the ID word goes round it
the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: identity documents are one's papers
the opening letter of many

explanation.surface: An identity check covers the first of many infants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Babies' looks like a plural noun (and Pampers are nappies), but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To baby someone is to coddle them, so 'babies' as a verb means pampers.

clue.text: Beetle and suchlike indoors can make super alarm go off

indicators.note: something that goes off explodes or spoils, so the letters break apart and reform

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, also part of the indicator phrase

explanation.surface: Beetles and other bugs in the house may set off a great alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' is not an insect but a dice game in which players draw a beetle part by part.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetle is a family dice game, one of many games played indoors that are called parlour games.

clue.text: Annual value long delayed holding large number up

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so the delayed word goes round the number
in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: later means delayed a long while; split to take the number
N stands for an indefinitely large number in maths
the rest of LATER

explanation.surface: A yearly valuation has been postponed for ages, holding a big figure up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental is the amount paid as rent, which is reckoned as a yearly sum or annual value.

clue.text: Nut's son opening flag

blocks.note: os is an anatomical term for an opening or mouth
a flag is an iris, the plant

explanation.surface: A crazy person's boy starts to lose heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' is not a madman but the Egyptian sky goddess, mother of Osiris. Flag here is the plant, not a banner or a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In Egyptian myth Osiris was a child of the sky goddess Nut and the earth god Geb.

clue.text: Divert noisy phones and one is unexpectedly dropping off

indicators.note: something that happens unexpectedly is out of its usual order
dropping something off means leaving it behind, so those letters go

blocks.note: taken as written; the answer's letters lying in order here is a coincidence, as the clue builds it by removal and rearrangement
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Redirect noisy phones, and someone suddenly falls asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To siphon or syphon off is to divert something, especially funds, to another use.

clue.text: Acreage retained in French city for milk producer

indicators.note: something retained in a place is held inside it

blocks.note: Brest is a port city in Brittany, opened to take the inserted letter
A is the abbreviation for acre or acreage
the rest of BREST

explanation.surface: Farmland in a Breton city is kept for dairy production.
explanation.definitionFit: A breast is the mammary gland, which produces milk.

clue.text: Mini-rugby ground not terribly big and not marshy

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
not says the following letters are excluded from the fodder
terribly says the removed word appears in scrambled form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A junior rugby pitch is not too large and not boggy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of big are scattered through mini-rugby, so they come out before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Miry means boggy or muddy, so unmiry means free of mire, not marshy.

clue.text: Return stake that's hotly tipped in Sicily

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the letters are read the other way

blocks.note: an ante is a poker stake

explanation.surface: A gambler gets back a bet on a hot favourite in Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotly tipped' sounds like racing, but the tip is a volcano's red-hot summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano of Sicily, whose summit glows with lava.

clue.text: Paper probing each trading group

indicators.note: a probe goes inside something, so the paper sits within the other word

blocks.note: EA is the abbreviation for each, opened to take the paper
the FT is the Financial Times
the rest of EA

explanation.surface: A financial newspaper investigates each member of a trade bloc.
explanation.definitionFit: EFTA is the European Free Trade Association, a trading bloc of European nations.

clue.text: Puffin identification in Iceland ends in breeding season

indicators.note: the ends of a phrase are its first and last letters only

blocks.note: IS is the international code for Iceland
the outer letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A puffin is identified in Iceland at the end of the nesting season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puffin' is not the seabird but Puffin Books, the children's paperback publisher.
explanation.definitionFit: An ISBN, International Standard Book Number, identifies each book a publisher such as Puffin issues.

clue.text: Gave instruction as audibly stressed

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word is judged by sound, not spelling

blocks.note: taught means gave instruction

explanation.surface: A teacher's voice showed the strain of lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A taut rope is pulled tight under tension, that is, stressed.

clue.text: Talk up a Chinese mustard

blocks.note: to talk something up is to praise it
taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for Chinese

explanation.surface: Promoting a Chinese mustard green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinese mustard' reads as one item, but Chinese ends the wordplay and mustard alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Praiseach is an Irish name for charlock, the wild mustard plant.

clue.text: Unfortunate bias shown in bash for eastern worshipper

indicators.note: an unfortunate word has come out badly, so its letters are disordered
shown in places these letters inside the beating word

blocks.note: to tan someone is to beat or bash them, opened to take the fodder
taken as written
the rest of TAN

explanation.surface: Regrettable prejudice is aired at a party for someone of an eastern faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' looks like a party, but it is the verb to beat, as is tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsabian is a variant of Sabian, a member of an ancient Middle Eastern star-worshipping religion.

clue.text: Strictly judge former boxer

blocks.note: first meaning: ... Tonioli, a judge on the TV dance show Strictly Come Dancing
second meaning: Frank ..., British heavyweight champion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Strictly' reads as an adverb telling you to judge harshly; it is the BBC dance contest Strictly Come Dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Two famous Brunos: Tonioli the dance show judge and Frank the retired heavyweight boxer.

clue.text: Unfashionable Asian satin in the end not finished

indicators.note: something not finished lacks its ending, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: at last means in the end

explanation.surface: An out-of-date Eastern fabric was eventually left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfashionable' marks the obsolete sense: atlas was once a name for a satin made in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas is an obsolete term for a silk-satin fabric originally made in Asia.

clue.text: PM gains weight

blocks.note: to gain something is to win it
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A prime minister puts on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: PM is Prime Minister: Winston Churchill, Britain's wartime leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was Britain's Prime Minister during World War II, known widely by his first name.
